governingStatute: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 read with Companies Act, 2013 Schedule III
statutorySection: Section 22 of MSMED Act, 2006 read with Section 23 of MSMED Act, 2006 and Schedule III Division I & II
title: Mandatory statutory disclosures in annual audited financial statements regarding dues to Micro and Small Enterprises and tax non-deductibility of penal interest

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Annual Financial Year-End Audited Financial Statements (March 31)

plainTextSummary: Section 22 of the MSMED Act, 2006 mandates that any buyer required to have its accounts audited under any law must furnish five specific disclosures in its annual financial statements regarding trade payables to micro and small enterprises: (1) Principal and interest due remaining unpaid at year-end, (2) Interest paid along with delayed payments made during the year, (3) Interest due and payable for delays without added interest, (4) Interest accrued and remaining unpaid at year-end, and (5) Further interest remaining due and payable in succeeding years. In parallel, Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013 prescribes a mandatory Trade Payables Aging Schedule segregating MSME dues (undisputed and disputed) into buckets: less than 1 year, 1-2 years, 2-3 years, and more than 3 years. Under Section 23 of the MSMED Act, compound penal interest payable or paid under Section 16 is strictly prohibited from being claimed as an income tax deduction, requiring an explicit book-to-tax add-back.

keyStatutoryThresholds.disputeSegregation: Mandatory separate aging disclosure for Undisputed MSME dues vs. Disputed MSME dues
keyStatutoryThresholds.taxAddbackMandate: Section 23 strictly disallows Section 16 penal interest under Income-tax Act, 1961 (and Act 2025)
keyStatutoryThresholds.statutoryAuditVerification: CARO 2020 Clause (xvi)(d) / (xix) requires statutory auditors to verify material uncertainty on settlement of MSME payables
keyStatutoryThresholds.applicableEntities: All corporate and non-corporate entities subject to statutory audit having transactions with registered Micro/Small enterprises
